explanation: The defect is in js::UncheckedUnwrapWithoutExpose (js/src/proxy/Wrapper.cpp). The real fix folds the exit conditions into the loop header so the null check covers every iteration: `while (wrapped && wrapped->is<WrapperObject>() && MOZ_LIKELY(!IsWindowProxy(wrapped)))`. My patch folds the conditions the same way but uses the broader `IsProxy(wrapped)` predicate instead of `wrapped->is<WrapperObject>()`, while the loop body still performs `wrapped->as<WrapperObject>().target()`. For a cross-compartment wrapper whose target is itself a non-wrapper scripted Proxy, the first iteration unwraps the CCW to the scripted Proxy; the second iteration passes the `IsProxy` guard (a scripted Proxy is a proxy but not a WrapperObject) and then calls `as<WrapperObject>()` on it, a type confusion. In the debug+ASan shell this fires the `MOZ_ASSERT(is<WrapperObject>())` inside `as<>()` (fatal signal); in a release build it is an out-of-type read of the proxy's reserved slot. The real upstream fix keeps the `is<WrapperObject>()` predicate, so it simply stops unwrapping at the scripted Proxy and returns it without crashing.

verification.parent_or_golden: On the pinned parent build (structurally identical to parent+golden for this input, since neither null nor forwarding is involved), `pocs/probe.js` prints 'no crash' and exits 0.
verification.edited_tree: On the rebuilt edited ASan shell, `/out/js --fuzzing-safe --no-threads --no-baseline --no-ion pocs/probe.js` aborts with a fatal assertion in JSObject::as<WrapperObject>() reached from UncheckedUnwrapWithoutExpose during the WeakMap delegate lookup.
